summary.headline: Consolidated EBITDA rose 144.94% YoY to INR155 crore and PAT more than doubled QoQ to INR61 crore as Punjab turned PAT positive.
summary.overview: Consolidated sales volume rose to 1.22 lakh MT from 96,000 MT in Q1 as the Punjab plant ramped up and customers returned to normal buying after deferring purchases in Q1. Consolidated revenue grew 35% QoQ to INR1,804 crore and EBITDA rose 43% QoQ to INR155 crore, with EBITDA per ton up 13% to INR12,725. Depreciation and finance costs rose only about INR5 crore QoQ, so most EBITDA gain reached PAT. Standalone EBITDA of INR84 crore was 11.7% below Q1 as spreads normalised and inventory gains were absent. Technical textiles capacity at Silvassa doubled to 18,000 MTPA from 20 August 2026.

segments.name: Silvassa (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sold about 58,000 MT vs 52,000 MT in Q1; utilisation about 95%. Q1 benefited from low-cost inventory gains, so Silvassa EBITDA fell about 11% QoQ. Product mix: polyester 77%, cotton about 18%, technical textiles about 6%.

segments.name: Punjab
segments.commentary: Sold about 64,000 MT in Q2; phase one fully operational at 700 MT/day polymerisation capacity with utilisation above 90% (vs about 76-77% in Q1). Plant turned PAT positive this quarter.

segments.name: Technical textiles (Silvassa)
segments.commentary: Capacity doubled from 9,000 to 18,000 MTPA on 20 August 2026; utilisation of new capacity about 94-95%. Management expects about INR80-90 crore incremental revenue in FY27 and INR150-160 crore annualised.

segments.name: Consolidated product mix
segments.commentary: Polyester about 87% of consolidated revenue, cotton about 10%, technical textiles about 3%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue now expected above INR6,000 crore vs earlier target of INR5,600-5,700 crore; FY28 about INR7,200-7,300 crore; FY29 about INR7,700-8,000 crore.
FY27 EBITDA target raised to north of INR560 crore vs earlier INR520-550 crore (INR520-530 crore as stated in one question).
Punjab phase two (250 TPD, to 900 TPD total): first portion to commission around December 2026; full ramp-up to 900 TPD by June-July 2027. Punjab utilisation target 95-96% in the next two quarters.
Gross debt about INR1,350 crore and net debt about INR1,150 crore by FY27 end; gross debt to reduce by about INR120 crore in FY28.
Capex about INR200 crore in FY27 (remaining) and about INR400 crore in FY28, with some spill-over into FY29.
Silvassa exports expected to move to double digits in coming months on the EU FTA, versus 4-17% range historically.
capex_capacity: Punjab phase one (700 MT/day polymerisation) fully operational; utilisation above 90% in Q2.
Punjab phase two: 250 TPD addition, first part by December 2026, full 900 TPD by June-July 2027.
Silvassa technical textiles capacity doubled to 18,000 MTPA, commenced production 20 August 2026.
Proposed INR400 crore MP cotton yarn project: site work from early January 2027, production by end of calendar 2026, full stabilisation by FY27 end (per Q&A; management noted land position on track).
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as strong, though monthly movement uneven: some months high, some slow; annualised demand intact.
Customers who deferred purchases in April-May returned to normal buying in Q2; sales ran ahead of production.
Raw material pass-through to customers takes about two weeks; PTA price rise in October noted, crude correcting again.
Chinese FDY imports have been limited since BIS/QCO removal, as landed Chinese material is pricier than domestic and para-xylene supply to China is constrained.
EU FTA expected to give Bangladesh-disadvantaged Indian yarn, fabric and garment exports an advantage.
Around 5 MT of new PTA capacity from GAIL (this year), IOCL (1H CY27) and Reliance (about 2028); no major new polyester yarn capacity announced, implying about 2.5 years before new yarn supply.
Management did not confirm analyst's INR2-3/kg EBITDA savings estimate but expects margin uplift from lower raw material supply.

qa_highlights.question: Why have gross margins declined sequentially and YoY despite better polyester filament spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said absolute gross margin improved on a consolidated basis; percentage margin fell because selling prices rose, so the per-ton spread is a smaller percentage of a larger base.

qa_highlights.question: Silvassa volumes have slipped from about 60-62k MT to 57-58k MT; why, and was Q1 helped by inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman cited product-mix changes based on demand and netbacks. Q1 had a low-cost inventory benefit, absent in Q2, plus incremental expenses; Silvassa EBITDA about 11% lower QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to H2 EBITDA guidance given H1 margin of about 8.3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said to track EBITDA per ton, not percentage; Punjab EBITDA per ton was about INR2,500-3,000 in Q1 and will rise further as utilisation reaches 95-96%.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 and FY28 debt and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt about INR1,350 crore and net debt about INR1,150 crore at FY27 end; capex about INR200 crore in FY27 and about INR400 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is Silvassa export share and margin differential?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports ranged 4-5% to 16-17% of Silvassa sales depending on netbacks; with the FTA, exports expected to reach double digits. Margin differential is rotational and depends on netbacks.

qa_highlights.question: What is technical textile utilisation and incremental revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: New capacity at about 94-95% utilisation; about INR80-90 crore incremental FY27 revenue on roughly half a year of operation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on the MP cotton yarn project?
qa_highlights.answer: On track: site work from early January, production by end of calendar 2026, full stabilisation by FY27 end.

risks_watch: Crude and PTA volatility: October PTA rise and recent crude correction; pass-through lag of about two weeks.
Punjab phase two commissioning (December 2026) and ramp to 900 TPD by June-July 2027; execution risk.
Silvassa volume trend has declined over three quarters (about 62k to 58k MT); product-mix driven per management.
Guidance inconsistency on the call: FY27 EBITDA cited as INR520-530 crore, INR520-550 crore and north of INR560 crore; revenue cited as INR5,600-5,700 crore and above INR6,000 crore.
Gross margin percentage compression despite higher absolute gross margin.
Upcoming PTA capacity additions (GAIL, IOCL, Reliance) could ease raw material costs but also change spreads.
Fiscal FY28 capex of about INR400 crore and debt reduction plan of about INR120 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and Punjab scaling, with frequent upward revisions to revenue and EBITDA targets. Evasive when asked for margin percentages and H2 EBITDA bridge, redirecting to EBITDA per ton. Cautious on monthly demand and crude-driven price moves.
key_quotes: Consolidated EBITDA rose 43.2% sequentially and 144.94% year-on-year to INR155 crores.

I'm also pleased to share that our expanded technical textiles capacity at Silvassa commenced production on August 20th, 2026, doubling our installed capacity from 9,000 metric tons per annum to 18,000 metric tons per annum.
As far as Punjab is concerned, we are operating today at 700 TPD, and we are moving towards the second phase, which is 900 TPD.
The realization trend, see, barring some hiccup internationally, I don't see any major disturbance of the realization front.

growth.why: Management raised FY27 EBITDA to north of INR560 crore and FY27 revenue to above INR6,000 crore, backed by Punjab phase one at over 90% utilisation, phase two (250 TPD) commissioning from December 2026, and the doubled Silvassa technical textiles line; the brief gives no FY27 revenue growth percentage and no explicit numeric revenue growth for FY27.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Punjab EBITDA per ton was about INR2,500-3,000 in Q1 and should rise as utilisation goes from above 90% to the 95-96% target, while management expects margin uplift from lower raw material supply; consolidated EBITDA per ton already up 13% QoQ to INR12,725, though gross margin percentage fell as selling prices rose.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (Dec 2026); full 900 TPD by Q1 FY28
rows.why: Punjab phase two (250 TPD, to 900 TPD total) is under construction with first portion due around December 2026 and full ramp by June-July 2027, and Silvassa technical textiles already doubled to 18,000 MTPA from 20 August 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Consolidated volume rose to 1.22 lakh MT from 96,000 MT in Q1, Punjab sold about 64,000 MT with utilisation above 90% targeted at 95-96%, and technical textiles new capacity runs at about 94-95%; Silvassa volume fell to 58,000 MT from 62,000 MT over three quarters, so the gain is Punjab-led.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation above 90% with Punjab phase two already in progress; the proposed INR400 crore MP cotton yarn project is approved with site work from early January 2027, and FY28 capex of about INR400 crore is guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue raised to above INR6,000 crore from INR5,600-5,700 crore and FY27 EBITDA to north of INR560 crore from INR520-550 crore; management has raised targets repeatedly on the call, though the figures are inconsistent across the call.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Crude and PTA volatility with a two-week pass-through lag, Punjab phase two execution risk on the December 2026 and June-July 2027 timelines, and Silvassa standalone EBITDA down about 11.7% QoQ to INR84 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Technical textiles capacity doubled to 18,000 MTPA with about INR80-90 crore incremental FY27 revenue expected and INR150-160 crore annualised; no new branded product launches were discussed.

rows.label: Silvassa exports to double digits on EU FTA
rows.why: Exports have ranged 4-17% of Silvassa sales historically, and management expects double digits on the EU FTA, which gives Indian yarn, fabric and garment exports an advantage over Bangladesh.

rows.label: Gross debt down to about INR1,350 crore by FY27 end
rows.why: Net debt guided at about INR1,150 crore by FY27 end and gross debt to fall about INR120 crore in FY28, against FY27 capex of about INR200 crore and FY28 capex of about INR400 crore.

rows.label: Customer restocking after Q1 deferrals
rows.why: Customers who deferred purchases in April-May returned to normal buying in Q2, with sales running ahead of production, which lifted volumes to 1.22 lakh MT from 96,000 MT in Q1.
